rules.title: Never commit secrets, API keys, or credentials to version control
rules.summary: Keep all API keys, tokens, passwords, and private certificates in environment variables or secret managers, and ensure .env files remain gitignored.

examples.text: Never hardcode API keys, tokens, or secrets in source files; always read them from environment variables.
Always use secret placeholders in config examples and never paste live keys into code or logs.
Audit staged diffs before committing to ensure no secrets or bearer tokens are leaked.
Do not commit .env files, credentials, or private keys under any circumstances.

rules.title: Run tests, linter, and type-checker before marking a task complete
rules.summary: Always execute the repository's test suite, linter, and static type checks after making edits and resolve every failure before reporting completion.

examples.text: Before finishing any change, verify that lint, typecheck, and unit tests all pass with zero warnings.
Run pytest and ruff check on all touched modules before concluding your response.
Always run the full test suite and type-check command after modifying code; do not claim completion with failing checks.

rules.title: Read and understand existing code and conventions before editing
rules.summary: Inspect surrounding files, architectural patterns, and project conventions prior to proposing or applying changes so new code blends seamlessly.

examples.text: Explore the codebase first to reuse existing utilities and follow established naming conventions.
Never modify a file you have not read first; inspect existing patterns and imports before writing code.
Always check adjacent components and shared hooks before introducing new abstractions.

rules.title: Keep changes minimal, focused, and strictly scoped to the request
rules.summary: Avoid unrelated refactoring, formatting churn, or unsolicited feature additions outside the task boundary to keep diffs reviewable and safe.

examples.text: Make the smallest surgical change necessary; do not reformat untouched lines or refactor unrelated modules.
Stay strictly within the scope of the user request and avoid speculative abstractions.
Do not touch unrelated files or rename symbols outside the current ticket scope.

rules.title: Use strict static typing and avoid `any` or unsafe type casts
rules.summary: Prefer explicit interfaces, discriminated unions, and `unknown` with runtime narrowing instead of `any` or silencing compiler checks with `@ts-ignore`.

examples.text: Do not suppress type errors with `@ts-ignore` or `as any`; fix the underlying type definition.
Never use `any` in TypeScript; use `unknown` with type guards or explicit generic constraints.
All public functions must include complete type annotations and strict return types.

rules.title: Write unit and regression tests for every new feature and bug fix
rules.summary: Pair behavioral changes with targeted automated tests covering both happy paths and edge cases, reproducing bugs with a failing test first when possible.

examples.text: Add unit tests covering edge cases whenever introducing new business logic or API endpoints.
Every bug fix must include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after.

rules.title: Never silently swallow exceptions; handle or propagate errors explicitly
rules.summary: Avoid empty catch blocks. Log actionable context, return typed error results, or rethrow with clear messages so failures remain diagnosable.

examples.text: Never write empty catch blocks or silently ignore errors; either recover meaningfully or rethrow with context.
Surface actionable error messages with structured context instead of generic catch-all handlers.

rules.title: Write concise, atomic commits following Conventional Commits
rules.summary: Group logically related changes into small, self-contained commits with clear `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, or `docs:` prefixes.

examples.text: Write commit messages that explain why the change was made, not just which files changed.
Use Conventional Commits format (feat:, fix:, refactor:, test:, docs:) and keep each commit atomic.

rules.title: Do not add new third-party dependencies without justification or approval
rules.summary: Prefer standard library APIs and existing packages already in the lockfile before introducing new external dependencies.

examples.text: Avoid adding new npm or PyPI dependencies when standard library or existing workspace packages suffice.
Always ask before installing new packages and never manually edit lockfiles.

rules.title: Never force-push, rewrite shared history, or run destructive git commands
rules.summary: Prohibit `git push --force`, `git reset --hard`, or `git checkout -- .` on shared branches unless explicitly authorized by the user.

examples.text: Never run destructive git commands like `git reset --hard` or `git push --force` without explicit confirmation.
Always work on a dedicated feature branch and never push directly to main.

rules.title: Validate and sanitize all external inputs at system boundaries
rules.summary: Enforce schema validation (e.g., Zod, Pydantic) on user input, API payloads, and query parameters, and use parameterized queries to prevent injection.

examples.text: Validate all incoming request payloads with Zod schemas and never interpolate untrusted input into SQL queries.
Sanitize user-supplied HTML and validate URLs before rendering or redirecting.

rules.title: Clarify ambiguous requirements instead of making silent assumptions
rules.summary: When specifications are underspecified or have meaningful trade-offs, state assumptions concisely or ask targeted clarifying questions before implementing.

examples.text: Outline a brief plan for multi-file changes and call out any assumptions explicitly.
If requirements are ambiguous or have multiple valid architectures, ask clarifying questions before writing code.

rules.title: Use the repository's configured package manager and virtual environment
rules.summary: Match the repo's lockfile (`pnpm`, `bun`, `uv`, `poetry`, etc.) and never mix package managers or install dependencies globally.

examples.text: Use `uv` for Python virtual environments and dependency resolution; never run global `pip install`.
Always use `pnpm` for installing packages and running scripts; never run `npm install` or `yarn`.

rules.title: Keep functions small, focused, and easy to reason about
rules.summary: Decompose complex logic into cohesive, single-responsibility functions with early returns to minimize nesting and improve testability.

examples.text: Prefer early returns and small pure helper functions over deeply nested conditionals.
Keep components and functions modular with a single clear responsibility.

rules.title: Write comments explaining why, not restating what the code does
rules.summary: Prefer self-documenting names for clarity and reserve comments for non-obvious invariants, edge cases, workarounds, and trade-offs.

rules.title: Always configure timeouts, retries, and backoff on external I/O
rules.summary: Set explicit request timeouts and bounded exponential backoff for HTTP calls and database connections to avoid hanging workers.

examples.text: Every outbound HTTP request must specify a timeout and handle 429/5xx responses with exponential backoff.

rules.title: Use semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, and WCAG-compliant contrast
rules.summary: Build interactive UI with native semantic elements (`<button>`, `<dialog>`, `<nav>`), visible focus rings, and proper ARIA labels.

examples.text: Always use native `<button>` and `<dialog>` elements with keyboard support and accessible names.

rules.title: Never fabricate file paths, APIs, or symbol names without verifying
rules.summary: Confirm every referenced file, function signature, and CLI flag directly in the workspace or official docs before citing or calling it.

examples.text: Verify that every imported module, file path, and API method actually exists in the repository before using it.

rules.title: Update README and docs when public APIs or CLI flags change
rules.summary: Keep usage examples, environment variable tables, and API docs accurate whenever modifying user-facing behavior or configuration.

examples.text: Whenever adding a CLI flag or environment variable, document it in README.md in the same PR.

rules.title: Never log PII, session tokens, or raw credentials in application logs
rules.summary: Redact authorization headers, passwords, and personally identifiable fields before writing structured logs or error reports.

examples.text: Redact Authorization headers, cookies, and user emails from all structured logs and Sentry breadcrumbs.

rules.title: Prefer immutable updates over mutating shared state in place
rules.summary: Avoid mutating function arguments or shared store objects directly; return new copies to prevent subtle state synchronization bugs.

examples.text: Do not mutate React state or function parameters in place; always return new objects or arrays.

rules.title: Pin CI action versions and container base images for reproducibility
rules.summary: Avoid floating `:latest` tags in Dockerfiles and unversioned GitHub Actions so builds remain deterministic and resistant to supply-chain drift.

examples.text: Pin all GitHub Actions to explicit major tags or commit SHAs and never use `:latest` in production Dockerfiles.

rules.title: Fail fast at startup when required configuration or env vars are missing
rules.summary: Validate required environment variables during initialization with clear error messages rather than failing lazily deep in request handlers.

examples.text: Validate all required environment variables at startup and exit immediately with a descriptive message if any are missing.

rules.title: Inspect full `git diff` and remove debug artifacts before opening a PR
rules.summary: Check staged changes for stray `console.log`, `print()`, temporary files, or unintended edits before committing or requesting review.

examples.text: Always review `git status` and `git diff` to strip debug logs and temporary files before committing.

rules.title: Load specialized SKILL.md workflows before improvising domain tasks

examples.text: When a matching SKILL.md exists for a task, read its instructions completely before executing commands.

rules.title: Batch independent file reads and searches in parallel to reduce latency
